newsitem.title: CANADA: Golden Rule sinks on Ghana assay reports.
newsitem.headline: Golden Rule sinks on Ghana assay reports.

text.p: Shares in Golden Rule Resources Ltd plummeted on Friday after check assays on its joint venture gold project in Ghana suggested original assays for the joint venture were overstated.
Golden Rule stock sank 3.46 to close at 3.94 in heavy turnover of 2.6 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Joint venture partner Hixon Gold Resources Inc was halted on the Vancouver Stock Exchange on Friday. The stock closed at 6.40 on Thursday.
Calgary-based Golden Rule said it received two reports on the project from the Ghana Minerals Commission earlier this week and passed them on to an independent mining consultant.
The results from the government studies showed less quantities of gold than that estimated by the joint venture.
During a conference call on Friday, Golden Rule President Glen Harper said differences could occur because of the coarse nature of the gold in the area.
Harper said he sympathized with shareholders worried about their investments.
"I'm there. I'm eating my own cooking. I have faith in the project," Harper said, adding that he owned almost two million shares of Golden Rule.
Associated Mining Consultants Ltd is expected to deliver a report to Golden Rule by mid-June. "We're very confident in their professional analysis and we'll get to the bottom of it," Harper said.
One of the government reports was prepared by a Vancouver-based consultant, CME Consulting Ltd. The other report was done by geological staff at the Minerals Commission.
